title: Understanding the Model
text: The model is given by the equation: $$\operatorname{f_{\theta}}\left(x\right)=0.5\theta_0+\theta_0 \theta_1 x_1+sin\left(\theta_1\right) x_2$$. This is a non-linear model with two parameters, $$\theta_0$$ and $$\theta_1$$.

title: Loss Function
text: The loss function for a single observation is given by: $$L(theta)=y_i-\operatorname{f_{\theta}}\left(x_i\right)$$. This means the loss is the difference between the actual value $$y_i$$ and the predicted value $$\operatorname{f_{\theta}}\left(x_i\right)$$.

title: Gradient Descent
text: Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm used to minimize the loss function. It updates the parameters $$\theta_0$$ and $$\theta_1$$ iteratively to find the optimal values that minimize the loss.

title: Initial Values
text: We start with initial values $${\theta_0}^0=0$$ and $${\theta_1}^0=0$$. What are the initial guesses for $$\theta_0$$ and $$\theta_1$$?

title: First Iteration Update
text: After the first iteration of gradient descent, we update the parameters. Use the gradient of the loss function to determine the new values for $${\theta_0}^1$$ and $${\theta_1}^1$$.
